_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Liberia covering indigenous Kru/Mande peoples, American Colonization Society settlement, Americo-Liberian dominance, True Whig Party era, Samuel Doe coup, Charles Taylor civil wars, Ebola crisis, and Ellen Johnson Sirleaf presidency.

ethnic_groups.notes: Largest indigenous group; central Liberia; Mande language; cross-border with Guinea

ethnic_groups.name: Bassa

ethnic_groups.name: Grebo

ethnic_groups.name: Gio/Dan
ethnic_groups.notes: Nimba County; Mande; Charles Taylor's base; cross-border with Ivory Coast-Guinea

ethnic_groups.name: Mano
ethnic_groups.notes: Nimba County; Mande; cross-border with Guinea; rebels in civil wars

ethnic_groups.name: Kissi

ethnic_groups.name: Gola

ethnic_groups.name: Vai

ethnic_groups.name: Mandingo/Mandinka
ethnic_groups.notes: Mande; Muslim traders; Lofa County; scapegoated during civil wars

ethnic_groups.name: Americo-Liberian/Congo
ethnic_groups.notes: Descendants of freed American slaves (1822 onwards) and recaptives; historically politically dominant; Monrovia elite; True Whig Party

independence.notes: Founded by American Colonization Society 1822; declared independence 1847; never formally colonized (with Ethiopia)

country_profile.notes_unique: Founded by freed American slaves in 1847; Africa's oldest republic; Ellen Johnson Sirleaf became Africa's first elected female head of state in 2006.

natural_resources.notes: ArcelorMittal iron ore mine at Yekepa; Firestone rubber plantation (one of world's largest); timber exports significant but deforestation concern; artisanal gold and diamond mining; offshore oil exploration.

military.notes: Armed Forces of Liberia (AFL) restructured by US after civil wars; UNMIL peacekeeping mission withdrew 2018; Coast Guard established with US support.

infrastructure.notes: Very poor road conditions; Lonestar, Orange operate; most infrastructure destroyed in civil war.

debt_aid.notes: HIPC debt relief 2010; heavily aid-dependent; US primary donor; post-war reconstruction ongoing; Ebola (2014-16) severely set back development.

education.notes: Education system devastated by 14 years of civil war; University of Liberia is Africa's oldest degree-granting institution; 2017 education reform act; teacher quality challenges.

diaspora_migration.notes: Large diaspora in US (Minnesota, Philadelphia, New York); many returned post-civil war; Ivorian refugees hosted during 2011 crisis.
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: ECOWAS free movement; refugee returns post-war

digital_economy.mobile_money_adoption: Emerging (Orange Money, Lonestar MTN Mobile Money)
digital_economy.notes: ACE submarine cable landed 2012; one of Africa's lowest internet penetration rates; mobile-first economy; digital financial inclusion growing slowly.

country_profile.national_motto: The Love of Liberty Brought Us Here

geography.terrain: Flat to rolling coastal plains; rolling plateau of dissected laterite; low mountains in northeast
geography.notes: Founded by freed American slaves (1847); oldest republic in Africa; Upper Guinean rainforest; Sapo National Park.

economy_extended.notes: Post-civil war recovery (1989-2003); iron ore, rubber, gold, timber, palm oil; world's largest ship registry (flag of convenience); dual currency (LRD/USD).

health.notes: Ebola devastated health system (2014-15, ~5000 deaths); rebuilding with international support; severe health worker shortage.

food_agriculture.notes: Rice main staple but 60% imported; Firestone rubber plantation historically dominant; palm oil traditional; post-war agricultural recovery slow.

energy.notes: Mt Coffee hydroelectric plant (88MW, rehabilitated 2016, USAID); one of lowest electricity access rates in world; diesel generators dominant.

transport.notes: World's 2nd largest ship registry (flag of convenience ~4000 vessels); very limited road network; no railway currently operational.

tourism.notes: Tourism undeveloped post-civil war; potential for beach and rainforest eco-tourism; Americo-Liberian heritage sites.

human_rights_gender.notes: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf (Africa's 1st elected female president, 2006-2018, Nobel Peace 2011); post-war reconciliation ongoing; Sande society (FGM cultural context).

security_stability.notes: UNMIL withdrew 2018; Joseph Boakai elected president 2023 (peaceful transition); post-civil war stability; SSR challenges remain.

cultural_heritage.media_landscape: FrontPage Africa; Daily Observer; ELBC state; private stations growing; vibrant talk radio
cultural_heritage.notes: Founded by freed American slaves (1847); unique Americo-Liberian/indigenous dynamic; only African country never colonized by European power.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Anglo-American common law and customary law
legal_system.customary_law_role: Applied in hinterland through statutory courts
legal_system.notes: Constitution modeled on US; dual legal system; Truth and Reconciliation Commission (2009) recommendations partially implemented.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.

current_leader.name: Joseph Boakai
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Unity Party; previously VP under Sirleaf 2006–2018; defeated George Weah 2023

former_leaders.name: William Tubman
former_leaders.notes: 27-year presidency; True Whig Party; Open Door Policy; unification of interior; longest-serving Liberian president; died in office

former_leaders.name: William Tolbert
former_leaders.notes: Last Americo-Liberian president; True Whig Party; assassinated in 1980 coup; Rice Riots 1979

former_leaders.name: Samuel Doe
former_leaders.notes: Master Sergeant; first indigenous president; Krahn; overthrew Tolbert; brutal rule; killed by Prince Johnson's rebels

former_leaders.name: Charles Taylor
former_leaders.notes: Warlord elected president; "He killed my ma, he killed my pa, but I will vote for him"; war crimes in Sierra Leone; exile in Nigeria; convicted by SCSL 2012; 50 years prison

former_leaders.name: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf
former_leaders.notes: Africa's first elected female head of state; Nobel Peace Prize 2011; post-war reconstruction; Ebola crisis 2014; economist

former_leaders.name: George Weah
former_leaders.notes: Only African to win FIFA World Player of the Year; CDC party; first peaceful democratic transition; economic struggles

910.name: Indigenous Peoples of the Pepper Coast
910.description: Migration and settlement of Kru, Mande, Mel, and other indigenous groups across the Grain/Pepper Coast region.

sub_clusters.name: Kru and Mande Migrations
sub_clusters.description: Successive waves of Mande-speaking and Kru-speaking peoples settle the forested Pepper Coast.

sub_clusters.name: Dei, Bassa, and Kpelle Societies
sub_clusters.description: Formation of decentralised chieftaincies; Poro and Sande secret societies shape governance and culture.

920.name: Pepper Coast Trade and European Contact
920.description: Malagueta pepper trade attracts Portuguese and other European traders; coastal exchange networks develop.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese Exploration of the Grain Coast
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese sailors trade for malagueta pepper and ivory; name the region 'Grain Coast'.

sub_clusters.name: European Trade Posts and Coastal Exchange
sub_clusters.description: Dutch, English, and French traders establish scattered factories; firearms and cloth for pepper, ivory, and captives.

930.name: Slave Trade on the Grain Coast
930.description: Transatlantic slave trade affects coastal and interior populations; Kru sailors become notable maritime labourers.

sub_clusters.name: Captive Trade and Coastal Raids
sub_clusters.description: European slavers extract captives; internal wars fuelled by demand; coastal communities disrupted.

sub_clusters.name: Kru Maritime Labourers
sub_clusters.description: Kru seamen hire onto European ships as skilled sailors; avoid enslavement through maritime bargaining power.

930.name: American Colonization Society and Settlement
930.description: ACS founded to resettle free Black Americans; Monrovia established 1822; settler-indigenous tensions.

sub_clusters.name: Founding of the American Colonization Society
sub_clusters.description: ACS created 1816 by Robert Finley and others; first settlers arrive at Cape Mesurado 1822.

sub_clusters.name: Founding of Monrovia
sub_clusters.description: Jehudi Ashmun leads colony; Monrovia named after President Monroe; settler governance established.

sub_clusters.name: Commonwealth of Liberia
sub_clusters.description: Thomas Buchanan as governor; Commonwealth status; push toward full sovereignty.

940.name: Republic of Liberia and Americo-Liberian Dominance
940.description: Independence declared 1847; Americo-Liberian elite control politics; True Whig Party hegemony; Firestone concession.

sub_clusters.name: Declaration of Independence
sub_clusters.description: Liberia declares independence 26 July 1847; Joseph Jenkins Roberts first president; Africa's first republic.

sub_clusters.name: True Whig Party Hegemony
sub_clusters.description: True Whig Party monopolises power for over a century; indigenous majority excluded from governance.

sub_clusters.name: Firestone Rubber Concession
sub_clusters.description: Firestone obtains million-acre lease for rubber plantations; shapes Liberian economy and labour relations.

sub_clusters.name: League of Nations Forced Labour Scandal
sub_clusters.description: Christy Commission reveals government complicity in forced labour akin to slavery; President King resigns.

950.name: Tubman and Tolbert Presidencies
950.description: William Tubman's Open Door Policy; William Tolbert's reforms; growing indigenous dissent leading to 1980 coup.

sub_clusters.name: Tubman's Open Door Policy
sub_clusters.description: President Tubman attracts foreign investment; cosmetic unification policy; authoritarian control persists.

sub_clusters.name: Tolbert's Reforms and Rice Riots
sub_clusters.description: Tolbert attempts modernisation; 1979 rice riots reveal deep inequality; indigenous opposition grows.

950.name: Samuel Doe Coup and Civil Wars
950.description: Doe's 1980 coup ends Americo-Liberian rule; ethnic violence; Charles Taylor's NPFL insurgency; two devastating civil wars.

sub_clusters.name: Samuel Doe's 1980 Coup
sub_clusters.description: Master Sergeant Doe overthrows Tolbert; executes cabinet on beach; ethnic Krahn favouritism; authoritarian rule.

sub_clusters.name: First Liberian Civil War
sub_clusters.description: Charles Taylor's NPFL invasion from Côte d'Ivoire; Doe killed 1990; ECOMOG intervention; ~200,000 dead.

sub_clusters.name: Charles Taylor Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Taylor elected 1997; sponsors RUF in Sierra Leone; widespread human rights abuses; ICC indictment.

sub_clusters.name: Second Liberian Civil War
sub_clusters.description: LURD and MODEL rebel groups challenge Taylor; Accra peace agreement 2003; Taylor exiled to Nigeria.

960.name: Post-Conflict Reconstruction and Democracy
960.description: UN peacekeeping; Ellen Johnson Sirleaf's historic presidency; Ebola crisis; George Weah presidency; ongoing recovery.

sub_clusters.name: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Africa's first elected female head of state; Nobel Peace Prize 2011; post-war reconstruction and debt relief.

sub_clusters.name: Ebola Crisis in Liberia
sub_clusters.description: West African Ebola epidemic devastates Liberia; ~5,000 dead; overwhelms health system; international response.

sub_clusters.name: George Weah Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Football legend George Weah elected president 2017; struggles with corruption and economic stagnation.

sub_clusters.name: Boakai Presidency and Democratic Consolidation
sub_clusters.description: Joseph Boakai wins 2023 election; peaceful transfer of power; democratic maturation continues.
